outcome: Operative delivery for intrapartum fetal compromise
Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 314 singleton appropriate-for-gestational-age pregnancies that underwent elective induction of labor between 41+0 and 41+6 weeks and were delivered before 42+0 weeks
finding: Low CPR in appropriate-for-gestational-age late-term pregnancies undergoing elective induction of labor was associated with a higher risk of operative delivery for intrapartum fetal compromise without increasing the adverse perinatal outcome rate.
